## Hook

::: {.cr-section}

::: {#cr-s01 .carpe-slide .quarto-title-block}
```{=html}
<h1 class="title">How many are you carrying?</h1>
<div class="quarto-title-authors">
</div>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s01"}
Forty-one is the number of live projects on my registry, by actual count: grants in three different phases, two papers, a course, four datasets, the website, the admin folder. Most researchers carry a number like it, and nobody holds it in their head.
:::

::: {#cr-s02 .carpe-slide .big}
```{=html}
<p>41</p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s02"}
Forty-one, then. Count yours the same way, folder by folder, and the figure is rarely smaller than you expect. The question this page answers is what happens to a number that size when nothing is keeping track of it.
:::

::: {#cr-s03 .carpe-slide .medium}
```{=html}
<p>The loud ones eat the week</p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s03"}
The loud projects, the ones with a date, eat the week. The quiet ones, the ones that matter most and have no deadline precisely because nobody is forcing them, stop moving. This page is about one small habit that fixes that, and what it takes to set it up in a week. How Claude Code works inside is a separate subject; the walkthrough covers it.
:::

:::

## The card

::: {.cr-section}

::: {#cr-s04 .carpe-slide .medium}
```{=html}
<p>bob.md</p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s04"}
Every project gets one short Markdown file at its root, called bob.md. Six fields on it decide where the project lands in your day.
:::

::: {#cr-s05 .carpe-slide .power}
```{=html}
<div class="items">
<p><span class="off">deadline</span> <span class="off">effort</span> <span class="off">weekly hours</span> <span class="off">priority</span> <span class="off">importance</span> <span class="off">blocking</span></p>
</div>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s05"}
The six fields, together first, then one at a time.
:::

::: {#cr-s06 .carpe-slide .power}
```{=html}
<div class="items">
<p><span class="on">deadline</span> <span class="off">effort</span> <span class="off">weekly hours</span> <span class="off">priority</span> <span class="off">importance</span> <span class="off">blocking</span></p>
</div>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s06"}
The deadline.
:::

::: {#cr-s07 .carpe-slide .power}
```{=html}
<div class="items">
<p><span class="off">deadline</span> <span class="on">effort</span> <span class="off">weekly hours</span> <span class="off">priority</span> <span class="off">importance</span> <span class="off">blocking</span></p>
</div>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s07"}
The hours left, roughly.
:::

::: {#cr-s08 .carpe-slide .power}
```{=html}
<div class="items">
<p><span class="off">deadline</span> <span class="off">effort</span> <span class="on">weekly hours</span> <span class="off">priority</span> <span class="off">importance</span> <span class="off">blocking</span></p>
</div>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s08"}
The hours a week you can give it.
:::

::: {#cr-s09 .carpe-slide .power}
```{=html}
<div class="items">
<p><span class="off">deadline</span> <span class="off">effort</span> <span class="off">weekly hours</span> <span class="on">priority</span> <span class="off">importance</span> <span class="off">blocking</span></p>
</div>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s09"}
Priority: what you want worked on now.
:::

::: {#cr-s10 .carpe-slide .power}
```{=html}
<div class="items">
<p><span class="off">deadline</span> <span class="off">effort</span> <span class="off">weekly hours</span> <span class="off">priority</span> <span class="on">importance</span> <span class="off">blocking</span></p>
</div>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s10"}
Importance deserves a pause. It is how much the project matters, whether or not anything is due, and it is set by you, never by a date. It comes back later, because it is the field that saves the quiet projects.
:::

::: {#cr-s11 .carpe-slide .power}
```{=html}
<div class="items">
<p><span class="off">deadline</span> <span class="off">effort</span> <span class="off">weekly hours</span> <span class="off">priority</span> <span class="off">importance</span> <span class="on">blocking</span></p>
</div>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s11"}
Blocking: whether someone is waiting on you. That bumps the project up a level and badges it.
:::

::: {#cr-s12 .carpe-slide .power}
```{=html}
<div class="items">
<p><span class="off">deadline</span> <span class="off">effort</span> <span class="off">weekly hours</span> <span class="off">priority</span> <span class="off">importance</span> <span class="off">blocking</span></p>
</div>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s12"}
That is all six. Under them sit three short sections: what you are doing this week, the next milestones, and a note called Start Here Next Session.
:::

::: {#cr-s13 .carpe-slide .medium}
```{=html}
<p>Start Here Next Session</p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s13"}
Start Here Next Session is the first thing your next session reads. Ten lines at most, rewritten every time. It is the handoff from you to the you of tomorrow, or to a teammate.
:::

::: {#cr-s14 .carpe-slide .big}
```{=html}
<p>150</p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s14"}
The card stays under a hundred and fifty lines. It describes the present only. What happened goes into a dated log; how to work in the project goes into the instructions file. Bob prunes the card every time it updates one, so it cannot grow into a diary.
:::

::: {#cr-s15 .carpe-slide .medium}
```{=html}
<p>Not on the card? It didn’t happen.</p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s15"}
One rule holds everything up: if it is not on the card, it did not happen. A card that is not updated looks exactly like a project that did not move. Everything that follows is in service of keeping that one file honest.
:::

:::

## The day

::: {.cr-section}

::: {#cr-s16 .carpe-slide .power}
```{=html}
<div class="items">
<p><span class="off">/bob</span> <span class="off">/bob go</span> <span class="off">/bob update</span> <span class="off">/bob weekly</span></p>
</div>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s16"}
Four commands cover almost everything.
:::

::: {#cr-s17 .carpe-slide .power}
```{=html}
<div class="items">
<p><span class="on">/bob</span> <span class="off">/bob go</span> <span class="off">/bob update</span> <span class="off">/bob weekly</span></p>
</div>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s17"}
In the morning, in a hub session, type /bob. It reads every card in under a second and returns the day's hours, what is red, three or four focus tasks, and a line for the important thing nobody is chasing.
:::

::: {#cr-s18 .carpe-slide .power}
```{=html}
<div class="items">
<p><span class="off">/bob</span> <span class="on">/bob go</span> <span class="off">/bob update</span> <span class="off">/bob weekly</span></p>
</div>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s18"}
Pick the first project and type /bob go with its name. That copies a launch line. A new terminal tab, paste, enter, and a fresh session opens inside that project with its own instructions and a five-line pickup from its card.
:::

::: {#cr-s19 .carpe-slide .medium}
```{=html}
<p>A fresh session for every project</p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s19"}
Nothing from the last project comes along, which is the point. A session belongs to the folder it started in. Telling one session to go work somewhere else does not load that project's instructions or memory, and the old conversation stays behind.
:::

::: {#cr-s20 .carpe-slide .power}
```{=html}
<div class="items">
<p><span class="off">/bob</span> <span class="off">/bob go</span> <span class="on">/bob update</span> <span class="off">/bob weekly</span></p>
</div>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s20"}
Before closing that tab, /bob update. Bob writes what changed onto the card and moves the story into a log. Every session, no exceptions; this is the habit.
:::

::: {#cr-s21 .carpe-slide .power}
```{=html}
<div class="items">
<p><span class="off">/bob</span> <span class="off">/bob go</span> <span class="off">/bob update</span> <span class="on">/bob weekly</span></p>
</div>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s21"}
On Friday, /bob weekly: hours next week, what is red, what has quietly slipped, and two questions about meetings and deadlines it does not know about yet.
:::

:::

## Quiet projects

::: {.cr-section}

::: {#cr-s22 .carpe-slide .medium}
```{=html}
<p>Urgency is loud</p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s22"}
This is the part that matters most. Deadline pressure is arithmetic: hours left over hours a week, against weeks to the date. Red, yellow, green. That measures urgency, and urgency is loud.
:::

::: {#cr-s23 .carpe-slide .medium}
```{=html}
<p>Importance is a field</p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s23"}
Importance is a separate field, set by you, and Bob crosses the two. The project with high importance and no deadline gets surfaced in every briefing, on purpose, and the warning sharpens when it goes stale.
:::

::: {#cr-s24 .carpe-slide .quote}
```{=html}
<blockquote>
<p>Important, not urgent. Untouched 34 days. Zero hours a week. Reset?</p>
</blockquote>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s24"}
That line is from my own briefing this week, trimmed. The paper behind it feeds a manuscript due in December. Without the line it would have slid to January.
:::

::: {#cr-s25 .carpe-slide .medium}
```{=html}
<p>What looks wrong?</p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s25"}
Every briefing ends with the same three words: what looks wrong. Bob surfaces; you decide. Move things, defer them, kill them, and the next daily reflects it. It never makes the call for you.
:::

:::

## Together

::: {.cr-section}

::: {#cr-s26 .carpe-slide .medium}
```{=html}
<p>One card per project</p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s26"}
Shared projects keep one card, never one per person. The lead is the steward and owns the top of it: phase, deadlines, blockers. Everyone else has their own section and edits only that. Your daily shows your tasks, the project's state, and who is waiting on whom.
:::

::: {#cr-s27 .carpe-slide .medium}
```{=html}
<p>A mailbox, not an email thread</p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s27"}
Notes between people and their assistants go in a mailbox file in the project folder. One line each, append only, and what you have read is tracked on your own machine, so reading never causes a sync conflict.
:::

::: {#cr-s28 .carpe-slide .medium}
```{=html}
<p>Synced drive or git. Never both.</p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s28"}
One rule about where projects live, because it bites on day two. A project is on the synced drive or in a git checkout, never both. A git repository inside a syncing folder gets corrupted, because the sync client writes into it while git is working.
:::

::: {#cr-s29 .carpe-slide .medium}
```{=html}
<p>Pull, then /bob</p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s29"}
The synced registry follows you between machines; a local one lists each machine's clones. Pull your clones before running the daily, because a stale clone shows a stale card. On the second machine, /bob scan says what is missing there.
:::

:::

## Close

::: {.cr-section}

::: {#cr-s30 .carpe-slide .big}
```{=html}
<p>5 <span class="label">minutes</span></p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s30"}
Five minutes to install: clone the repository, run the installer, add two lines to your settings file. The one-pager lists them.
:::

::: {#cr-s31 .carpe-slide .big}
```{=html}
<p>3 <span class="label">cards</span></p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s31"}
Three cards by Friday: open a project, type /bob add, answer roughly. About ten hours, two a week is plenty. Then the next project. Three is enough for the first daily to mean something.
:::

::: {#cr-s32 .carpe-slide .medium}
```{=html}
<p>Then type /bob</p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s32"}
Then type /bob. If the daily looks wrong, the card is wrong; fix the card. Fifteen minutes with the presenter is enough to get set up.
:::

::: {#cr-s33 .carpe-slide .medium}
```{=html}
<p>How many are you carrying?</p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s33"}
Back to the opening number. Everyone has one. Count how many of those projects have a card.
:::

::: {#cr-s34 .carpe-slide .medium}
```{=html}
<p>Three cards by Friday</p>
```
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-s34"}
Three cards by Friday. That is the whole ask.
